subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Grouping lexical items and describing a place
outcomes: Describe a town or village and ask questions about it
Understand how the SQU Rovers help new students

tf.s: When describing a place, you can talk about its location and features.
tf.why: These are sections of the plan.

tf.s: Asking questions after a talk shows interest.
A plan makes a description less clear.
tf.why: A plan organises information and makes it clearer.

tf.s: The SQU Rovers are a team of students who help new students.
tf.why: Yes, they help new students at SQU.

tf.s: A student who loses an ID card should go to the Administration Office.
tf.why: They report it there and get a replacement.

tf.s: The Rovers can only be found in the library.
tf.why: They are at stations such as the cafeteria or in front of the mosque.

tf.s: The Rovers tell homesick students that nobody else feels this way.
tf.why: They say everyone goes through the same thing.

tf.s: Finding their way around campus is a common problem for new students.
tf.why: A big campus can be confusing.

tf.s: Airport, passport, ticket and flight belong to the field of travel.
The new student in the picture looks confident and relaxed.
tf.why: He looks new, lost and confused.

boxes.q: Which sentence is about a town's location?
o: It is 20 km from the sea.
It has a beautiful old fort.
boxes.why: Location tells you where a place is.

boxes.q: Where do you report a lost ID card?
boxes.why: You can get a replacement there.

boxes.q: How does the student in the picture feel?
boxes.why: He is new and does not know where to go.

boxes.q: Why are questions useful after a talk?
What should you do after your partner's talk?
boxes.why: Asking questions keeps the conversation going.

o: How far is it from the sea?
boxes.why: Distance tells you where it is.

boxes.q: What do the Rovers say to homesick students?
boxes.why: They reassure them it will get better.

boxes.q: How does a plan help a description?
What is a common problem for new students?
boxes.why: The campus is new to them.

hunt.q: Students who help new SQU students
Report a lost ID card at the...
Card that shows you are a student
The student in the picture is...

mcq.q: What three things do you mention when describing a place?
o: Location, features and what people can do there
The names of all the people
mcq.why: These are the sections of the plan.

mcq.q: Why are new students sometimes upset?
o: They lose their ID cards and feel homesick
mcq.why: New students face many small problems.

mcq.q: Where can the Rovers be found?
o: At stations such as the cafeteria or in front of the mosque
mcq.why: They wait where new students can find them.

mcq.q: Which group of words is connected with travel?
Which question asks about the features of a town?
o: What famous buildings does it have?
How far is it from the sea?
How far is it from the capital?
mcq.why: Buildings are features; the others are about location.

mcq.q: A new student loses her ID card. What should she do?
o: Go to the Administration Office and get a replacement
Stay at home for a week
Ask the cafeteria for a new card
mcq.why: The Administration Office deals with ID cards.

mcq.q: You say: 'My town is on the coast, 50 km from Muscat.' Which section is this?
mcq.why: It tells where the town is.

mcq.q: How do the Rovers help with homesickness?
o: They say everyone goes through it and it will get better
mcq.why: Knowing others feel the same helps.

mcq.q: Why does a plan make a description clearer?
o: It organises information into logical sections

mcq.q: Why might it help that the Rovers are students themselves?
o: They have had the same experiences as new students
They know nothing about the university
